traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria for 010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION appear to be fully met: - Core functionality: The valid-req-reference rule reads the target story file, extracts all REQ-*-style identifiers, and verifies that each referenced @req or @supports requirement ID exists in that file. Tests cover both matching and non-matching scenarios. - Quality standards: Validation is agnostic to markdown structure and list markers, working for plain text, bullet lists, and multi-story fixtures. The bullet-list fixture and multi-story fixtures, plus the generic REQ-* regex, demonstrate support for varied requirement formats and story structures. - Integration: The rule integrates into the existing plugin exports and recommended/strict configs, cooperates with the established annotation styles (@story/@req and @supports), and reuses the same path-safety expectations as the file validation story. Config and plugin setup tests confirm this integration. - User experience: Error messages for missing requirements (reqMissing) and invalid paths (invalidPath) are specific and include both the problematic requirement ID and story path. Tests assert exact messageId and data payloads. - Error handling: Story files that cannot be read or are malformed are handled via try/catch in loadAndCacheRequirements, preventing crashes and resulting in consistent reqMissing diagnostics rather than hard failures. Path traversal and absolute paths are explicitly rejected with invalidPath diagnostics. - Documentation: docs/rules/valid-req-reference.md and references in user-docs/api-reference.md document the deep validation behavior, including how story files are parsed, how @req and @supports interact, error conditions, and concrete examples.
Given the concrete implementation, passing tests directly tied to this story, and comprehensive rule documentation, this story is assessed as PASSED.
